RestoreFeedback.scope: One submitted request and original restore identity, one body dispatch, and at most two distinct feedback generations. Unbounded feedback history; this model uses two generations.

MaintenanceApply.scope: Three ordered children represent two native reference allocations and one bound body. Binding dispatch, provider application, durable ACK and exact original allocation verification precede the body. Child dispatch, response, outcome and parent progress remain separate. Original local authority and a completely unissued suffix are required; unknown bindings and bodies are never replayed. No CAS or atomic multi-page claim. Known original failures settle as partial only after review.
excluded: Every native POST/PATCH/Record subrequest; narrower recovery models apply only to their named protocols
Same-execution lifecycle-event ACK/query union, provider index visibility and per-Record crash persistence
Known versus unknown native file modes, exact byte reconstruction and dry-run preview validation

An edit after a completed pre-dispatch observation; real readback and failure tests remain required
Raw Markdown/bytes, resource formats, reference rewrite parsing and permissions
Arbitrary plan length, all provider scopes and subsequent legitimate author changes after completion
The explicit body-review proof documents, byte hashes, compact plan storage and logical/native link projections are guarded by implementation regressions, not represented as string state.
